title: Redwood migration demo: OpenAI/Anthropic/Together parity mapping
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Novus Health through a migration/demo focused on API parity from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood. Covered mapping of models and parameters, console features for routing and rollouts, observability, and Optimize recommendations for reducing token cost and latency. Discussed security (SOC 2, VPC, KMS) and POC scope. Action items: send parity spreadsheet, SOC2 + network diagram, propose POC timeline and pricing options.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Khan (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Dana Ortiz (Novus Head of ML), Mike Patel (Novus Eng Manager), Sara Li (Novus CTO)

Auto-summary (auto): Redwood migration + POC scoping for moving from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API.

[00:00] Aisha Khan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Dana Ortiz: Dana here.
[00:07] Mike Patel: Mike on from infra.
[00:08] Sara Li: Sara here.
[00:09] Aisha Khan: Great. Liam from our SE team will lead the parity mapping and demo. We'll go ~45 minutes demo, then 15 for POC and next steps.

[00:38] Liam Chen: Yep hi all. I'll start with the high level — our goal today is to show how calls from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together map to Redwood API, what changes (if any) to prompts or params, and then jump into the Console and Optimize suggestions to lower cost. I'll try to show a sample benchmark run as well.

[01:15] Dana Ortiz: Major thing for us: we use GPT-4o (OpenAI) and Claude 3 (Anthropic) in prod. Latency is critical, and we have PHI so private network is a must. We need parity in output and the same tool-calling patterns. Also, token cost matters, we're looking for 20-30% savings.

[01:46] Liam Chen: Understood. On parity mapping: OpenAI-style completion/chat calls map to Redwood's /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints. Model names: conceptually you can map GPT-4o -> rwd-gpt4o-v1 (we'll send the exact mapping sheet), Claude 3 -> rwd-claude3-ish, and Together models similarly. Note: exact tokenizer differences can cause token counts to shift a bit so we'll include tokenization diffs.

[02:25] Sara Li: When you say 'rwd-gpt4o-v1' is that a drop-in replacement for our SDK calls? We try to keep minimal code change.

[02:38] Liam Chen: Yes, minimal changes. Most customers update the base URL + model name and a couple of param names. We support OpenAI-compatible request shapes and also have SDK helpers for languages. We'll share examples in the parity sheet and a migration gist.

[03:05] Mike Patel: What about streaming? We require streaming for chat.

[03:10] Liam Chen: Streaming is supported. We have SSE/http streaming and websockets in SDKs. Behavior is the same but we do have slightly different chunking semantics in some models — in practice it's near identical.

[03:40] Dana Ortiz: Ok, security: VPC or private deployment is non-negotiable for PHI. SOC2 is needed, and we need KMS/HSM key control.

[03:50] Aisha Khan: Yes, Redwood Private is designed for that. We offer a private control plane with customer-managed VPC peering or on-prem option. We support KMS integration and audit logs. I'll attach SOC2, the network diagram, and KMS docs after this call.

[04:20] Liam Chen: Quick Console demo — opening the Console. (screen shares) Top left: model catalog, you can pin versions and configure rollout policies. Route-by policy lets you send traffic to hosted vs dedicated, or fallback when capacity constrained.

[05:05] Liam Chen: Here is a route we commonly recommend for migrations: 80% to the Redwood-verified variant (lower cost opt), 20% to full-precision for QA. You can create canary rollouts and automatic rollbacks if quality drops.

[05:40] Dana Ortiz: That sounds good. How do you measure quality regressions? We need automated checks against prompt sets.

[05:48] Liam Chen: We integrate with Redwood Optimize — you can upload prompt sets and baselines. Optimize runs periodic evals, shows regression alerts, and ties them to specific model versions. It also suggests quantization profiles if accuracy is within threshold.

[06:20] Mike Patel: Do we need to change prompts for better cost? We already have prompt engineering and prefix system messages.

[06:28] Liam Chen: In many cases no. But Optimize will flag long system messages, high temperature settings, or redundant context that add tokens. It suggests batching and prefix caching — note the KV cache is managed by runtime, that reduces repeated prefix costs.

[07:05] Sara Li: What about latencies — we currently average ~220ms tail per request. Can you meet that?

[07:12] Liam Chen: Depends on model choice and deployment mode. For hosted with autoscale you can see good p50 but p95 may vary. Dedicated GPUs with pinned capacity and kernel selection are how you get consistent sub-200ms tails for smaller-ish models. We'll propose Dedicated configs in pricing.

[07:45] Dana Ortiz: Benchmarks matter — can you run a POC with our prompt set and traffic to validate latency and cost?

[07:52] Aisha Khan: Absolutely. For POC we usually do a 2-week run: initial ingest of prompt set, run benchmark on hosted vs dedicated pools, and then share results. Liam will draft the runbook.

[08:20] Liam Chen: Quick note about tokenization differences — OpenAI vs Anthropic tokenizers can shift counts up to ~8-10% on certain inputs. We include tokenization maps in the parity sheet and also show cost-normalized comparisons.

[08:55] Mike Patel: How about function/tool calling compat with what we've built? We use json-schema tool calls.

[09:02] Liam Chen: Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured output. We have a couple of different shapes but support the common json schema pattern. In some cases you may need to rename a field or change how content is wrapped; we'll show a migration snippet.

[09:35] (25 min demo screenshots and live console walkthrough, several short pauses that aren't fully transcribed)
[10:45] Liam Chen: Now the Optimize tab: here's a cost breakdown by token and by model. You can set cost limits and get recommendations for quantizing to int8/4 depending on tolerance. Remember quantizashun may slightly shift output so Optimize recommends tests.

[11:20] Dana Ortiz: We need cryptographic key control. How does KMS integration work?

[11:30] Liam Chen: We support customer-managed KMS in Private. For hosted accounts we offer KMS envelope encryption and rotation. For Private we can integrate with your KMS or HSM to control model keys and logs; details in the SOC2 + network doc.

[12:05] Mike Patel: Networking — what's required for VPC peering or on-prem? Ports, firewall rules?

[12:12] Aisha Khan: We'll provide a network diagram with CIDRs, peering steps, and firewall example. For peering you typically allow outbound to Redwood control plane and peering for data plane. Exact rules depend on Private vs Dedicated.

[12:40] Sara Li: SLA concerns — we need 99.9 for production. Do you offer SLA for Dedicated?

[12:47] Aisha Khan: Yes, Dedicated comes with SLA options. For hosted API we have best-effort but offer higher tiers and enterprise packages. We'll include SLA language in the contract options packet.

[13:10] Dana Ortiz: Cost ask — can you model expected monthly and per-token cost if we move everything, or hybrid?

[13:18] Aisha Khan: We'll run cost modeling. For hybrid we can route cold traffic to lower-cost quantized variants and hot paths to full-precision; Console routing rules make that easy. Liam will include sample cost scenarios in the pricing doc.

[13:45] Mike Patel: Any gotchas we should be aware of if we move quickly?

[13:50] Liam Chen: Main items: tokenization diffs, minor prompt tweaks, and performance tuning (batching, KV cache size). Also for function calling, ensure tool schemas align. We'll include migration snippets.

[14:12] Sara Li: Timeline — if we wanted to start POC next week, is that feasible?

[14:17] Aisha Khan: We can start onboarding in 1-2 weeks after initial docs and access are shared, POC kickoff target week of 2026-04-27 is realistic.

[14:40] Dana Ortiz: Ok good. For the POC we'll need an NDA'ed environment and clear data handling — we can't send PHI to hosted unless Private is in place.

[14:50] Aisha Khan: Understood. For PHI we'd recommend Private or dedicated with VPC and specific data retention rules. We'll work with legal to confirm.

[15:10] (wrap-up)
[15:12] Aisha Khan: Recap: Redwood to send parity mapping sheet, SOC2 and network diagrams, and pricing options. Novus to share prompt set + traffic profile. POC kickoff target week of 4/27. Any final Qs?
[15:30] Dana Ortiz: None from me.
[15:32] Mike Patel: None.
[15:33] Sara Li: Thanks all.
[15:34] Aisha Khan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up by Friday.

End of transcript.
